diagnostics.message: :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda: explicit depends_on of :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.forge_trust_validator_lambda already depends on aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda implicitly via `logging_log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda.name`; the explicit `depends_on = [aws_cloudwatch_log_group.forge_trust_validator_lambda]` duplicates that edge.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda already depends on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda implicitly via `arn = module.forge_trust_validator_lambda.lambda_function_arn`; the explicit `depends_on = [module.forge_trust_validator_lambda]` duplicates that edge.

null_resource.update_forge_role_trust updates each forge role's trust policy to grant the lambda execution role (arn:...:role/${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator) sts:AssumeRole, but it has no dependency on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda which creates that role. The trust update can run before the trusted lambda role exists, so the relationship should be ordered after the module.
